office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Two-term Republican Rep. Kevin Waters, a former Port of Skamania commissioner, faces Democrat Ben Christly, a Navy veteran and flight nurse on the county charter review commission. Waters has voted against the 2025 and 2026 tax bills and the operating budget; Christly campaigns on school funding and asking large corporations to pay more.

candidates.summary: Navy veteran, flight nurse and former small-business owner who sits on the elected Clark County Charter Review Commission, running on school funding, early learning, housing and health-care access.
highlights: Says working families and small businesses carry too much of the tax burden while "billion-dollar corporations" avoid theirs [S2]
Wants to fully fund public schools and expand preschool, pre-kindergarten and trade programs [S2]
Elected Clark County Charter Review Commissioner; first run for the Legislature [S5][S1]
Endorsed by the Washington Education Association PAC, the state labor council, Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Pro-Choice Washington [S4]

taxes.basis: Calls for a 'fair and responsible tax structure' in which large corporations pay more and working families less; no position on the income tax over $1 million.

spending.basis: Defines responsible budgeting as investing in schools, health care and economic opportunity, including fully funding schools and expanding early learning.

social.basis: No direct statement; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Pro-Choice Washington.

experience.basis: First legislative run; his only office is an elected seat on the county charter review commission, against a two-term incumbent.

candidates.summary: Two-term Republican incumbent from Stevenson, executive director of the Skamania Economic Development Council and founder of Backwoods Brewing, running on infrastructure, schools and public safety.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 and the 2025 capital gains, excise and B&O tax bills [S3][S5][S6][S7]
Offered an amendment to expire the 2025 services taxes on July 1, 2026; it failed 42-53 [S4]
Voted against the 2025-27 operating budget and says the state has "a results problem" [S8][S15]
Voted against rent-increase limits, the clean fuels expansion and ESHB 1296's changes to the parental-rights law [S9][S10][S11]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and three 2025 revenue bills, sponsored an amendment to expire the 2025 services taxes, and his campaign site promises tax cuts.

spending.basis: Voted twice against the 2025-27 operating budget and criticized spending past $80 billion, while also faulting the majority's education cuts.

housing.basis: Voted against limits on rent and fee increases (EHB 1217); pamphlet backs 'practical solutions' to expand affordable housing.

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement; campaign site calls for fully funding police and giving them tools for the fentanyl crisis.

climate.basis: Voted against the 2025 clean fuels program bill (2SHB 1409) on House passage and final passage.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296, which changed the parental rights enacted by Initiative 2081; no position on I-1 found.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2023 and Port of Skamania commissioner 2010-2019; challenger has not held legislative office.
